A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CompMarkGS with the same research objective, authors, and core pipeline. All pages, including figures and tables, support comparison. The supplied v4 ends after its references; v6 includes Appendices A–G, which were also inspected.

before.justification: Section 5 and Tables 1–7 report original rendering-quality, watermark-accuracy, compression, robustness, capacity, and ablation results.

after.justification: Section 5 retains original empirical results, while Appendices E–G add ablations, robustness experiments, rendering-speed measurements, and qualitative outputs.

M1.justification: The stated HSV objective changes from averaging color-specific losses normalized by N_c in v4 Eq. 11 to a shared |C||Omega| denominator in v6 Eq. 8; Appendix C.6 identifies Omega as the image domain. This is a localized revision of the reported loss specification. The bounded additive watermark feature, QDL, frequency-aware anchor growing, decoding pipeline, and other loss components remain.

E1.justification: The same 25 Blender, LLFF, and Mip-NeRF 360 scenes remain the reconstruction benchmarks. However, v6 substantially expands evaluated attack environments through LightGaussian pruning-based compression, general float32-to-int8 quantization, and decoder-targeted PGD attacks in Appendices E.3–E.4. These scenarios extend the original image distortions, random model manipulations, and two anchor-based compression schemes.

E2.justification: The original WateRF, GaussianMarker, and 3D-GSW comparators remain. v6 adds GuardSplat to the compression, distortion, and capacity comparisons, including Tables 1–3 and 12–13. Appendix D.1 explains its adaptation from explicit spherical-harmonic offsets to anchor-feature offsets. This is a bounded expansion of the watermarking comparator set; LightGaussian serves as a compression attack.

E3.justification: The attribute ablation changes from HAC before compression in v4 Table 6 to both HAC and ContextGS after compression in v6 Table 4. Component controls are also redesigned. New protocols include 66% LightGaussian pruning, int8 quantization, PGD with epsilon 0.1, an alternative SSL decoder, compression-strength sweeps, and FPS evaluation. v6 also aligns image-noise prose with sigma 0.1, already specified in v4's table; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v6 adds dedicated embedding-feature removal, alternative-decoder testing, HSV artifact visualizations, attack-strength sweeps, compression-level analysis, and additional compression/adversarial robustness tests. Its Table 5 replaces v4's FAG/HSV/frequency-loss combination study with individual FAG/QDL/HSV removals after both compression schemes, incorporating the earlier HAC QDL comparison. The earlier frequency-loss ablation is no longer reported.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. Results remain point estimates or averages across datasets and compression schemes. Gaussian-noise standard deviations specify attacks, not experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: The headline CompMarkGS values in Table 1 are retained, but HAC+3D-GSW post-compression bit accuracy changes from 46.52% to 53.48%. Other entries change, and substantial results are added for GuardSplat, revised ablations, attack sweeps, alternative decoding, and FPS. New examples include 90.11% accuracy after int8 quantization and 84.33% after PGD. These are newly reported settings, not improvements over matched v4 experiments.

T1.justification: The HSV-loss normalization receives a limited mathematical revision between v4 Eq. 11 and v6 Eq. 8. The central feature-addition, quantization-noise, high-pass-filter, and SSIM-error constructions otherwise match across renumbering and relocation. Appendix C largely formalizes previously described masks and supplies parameter definitions; neither version presents new theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution—compression-robust watermarking through anchor features, QDL, and frequency-aware growing—is retained. v6 adds a specific introductory claim that implicit MLP-generated attributes make watermark detection and manipulation difficult, and explicitly claims suitability for resource-constrained devices. v4's assertion of achieving the highest compression rate and efficiency is dropped.

C2.justification: v6 substantially expands mechanism explanations: tanh versus sigmoid bias, conflicts between low-frequency watermarking and quality optimization, median-based rejection of outlier influence, and color artifacts in sparsely represented regions. Appendices D–E add security arguments and interpretations of pruning resilience and decoder independence. The pretrained-decoder limitation is retained and expanded in Appendix B, rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents 30,000 training iterations, the 1,600–15,000 anchor-growing interval, conventional-to-frequency-aware growing, MS-COCO decoder pretraining, the stated compression setting of 0.004, gradient/opacity thresholds, and explicit HSV ranges and thresholds. Appendix D.1 documents GuardSplat's adaptation. These substantially improve implementation disclosure; they do not establish changes to previously unspecified training settings.

R1.justification: v6 substantially revises positioning by distinguishing steganography from ownership watermarking and adding a detailed comparison with SecureGS in Appendix D.1. It also expands distinctions from 3D-GSW and GuardSplat and discusses additional compression research such as CAT-3DGS and PCGS. Earlier coverage, including CopyRNeRF, is removed. These changes extend beyond bibliography formatting.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method rationale, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Preliminaries are shortened, technical explanations are reorganized between the main text and appendices, limitations move to Appendix B, and ethics, discussion, and implementation sections are added. The narrative restructuring is substantial.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with redesigned and relocated displays. v4 Table 2 becomes the expanded appendix Table 12, accompanied by new radar plots in v6 Figure 4. Ablation tables are restructured, GuardSplat is added to qualitative comparisons, and new HSV visualizations, robustness curves, compression-size plots, and multi-scene image panels substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v6 substantially reduces important documentation and validation gaps: Appendix C supplies implementation details absent from the supplied v4, and the revised ablations test components after both compression schemes. Additional robustness, decoder, and efficiency experiments strengthen assessment of the central compression claim. Reporting weaknesses remain: PGD settings are incomplete, and Appendix E.4 incorrectly calls GaussianMarker the strongest ContextGS baseline despite Table 11 reporting WateRF at 90.36% versus 87.95%. Neither version reports statistical uncertainty. These limitations temper the expanded claims but do not outweigh the substantial gains in reproducibility and empirical support.
